items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1959-11-08
items.q: No, I never did play with, Boccage

ctx.x: Yeah, he came from over the river. He used to live on, I tell you where he used to live, he used to live on, over the track there, he's right there on, Frank Boyle's got a garage, right across the street there. That's Hancock's. Yeah. That's Hancock's.
Well I was going to ask about some of the other musicians over there. Did you ever play with Peter Boccage much? Any of the Boccage brothers?

No, I never did play with, Boccage, yeah, I had a boy who used to play with me, play saxophone. Oh that's right, I heard him once with you. Yeah, Wilford Boccage, he played with me. His brother Leonard Boccage, he played banjo with me too once. He didn't play that long with me. Well he used to play with Son Allen. Yeah. See, he used to play with Son Allen then, you see.

items.title: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan…
items.q: There's range from Peter Boccage who plays a more subdued, a more quiet type music, quiet for jazz anyway.

ctx.x: Were you able to discern which bands are better than others? I mean, do you sort of say to someone, thank you, we don't want you anymore? We haven't had to. In other words, they're all of a pretty good quality then.

Well, each band, as my wife said, there are 20 and each one is different. It's, the quality is certainly different. And I think the musical idea that the people are trying to get across is different also. There's range from Peter Boccage who plays a more subdued, a more quiet type music, quiet for jazz anyway. Maybe a little more sophisticated than a person, a kid Thomas. Yeah. Where a kid Thomas is, is a lot, maybe rougher, a lot more direct.
Well, Alan, do you, this music is very exciting music and do you ever have any trouble with the crowds pushing in, with the crowds creating a riot, anything like this? Sort of.
